matches.sum: Bayern at home to Köln, with a side from the very top or bottom of the table involved. A competitive game for long stretches with around three expected goals between them. Solid rather than special – the highlights tell the story.

w: Stakes (top-two/bottom-two team, both top four/bottom four)
matches.sum: A meeting with plenty at stake at the table's extremes. Busy from start to finish: about 3.3 expected goals, a red card, a penalty and a VAR intervention, and the momentum keeps shifting. One of the round's livelier games – worth watching in full.
Athletic host Espanyol in San Mamés. A tight, cautious affair with few clear openings and little incident. The highlights are more than enough.
Elversberg against Freiburg. A close, hard-fought game without many chances, plus a goal ruled out along the way. Fine for the highlights.
Frankfurt against Hoffenheim, and plenty happens: around 4.6 expected goals, two penalties, a red card and a disallowed goal. Chances at both ends and the contest stays close – a good one to watch.

The Borussia derby at Mönchengladbach, with a side from the top or bottom two involved. Not many chances, but the derby edge is there and it stays tight. Stick with it – the final quarter of an hour is the part to see.
Leverkusen host Paderborn. Plenty of chances – around 4.6 expected goals combined – but the game never quite becomes a contest you need to see in full. Highlights recommended.
Schalke against Stuttgart, with a team from the top or bottom two involved. More than four expected goals and a close contest, though it rarely catches fire. Average – highlights are enough.

Union host Leipzig at the Alte Försterei. A very open game – around seven expected goals combined – with a penalty, a VAR intervention and the momentum swinging back and forth. Worth watching, especially the second half.
Lens against Toulouse at Bollaert. A competitive game with around 3.2 expected goals and both sides having their spells. Decent viewing, but the highlights cover it.
Lille host Lyon, with a team from the top or bottom two involved. A close, careful game with a goal ruled out and not much else. Highlights only.
Monaco against Auxerre. Close for most of the way with about 2.7 expected goals, and the closing stages are clearly the best part. Watch the highlights, or skip straight to the last twenty minutes.

In-form Nice, with four wins from their last five, host a PSG side among the top two and arriving on a five-match winning run. Around 2.7 expected goals and 18 shots between them, a penalty and a VAR intervention. It stays tense right to the end.
Strasbourg against Brest. A close game with around 3.3 expected goals, a penalty and a VAR intervention. Average overall – the highlights do the job.
Alavés host Deportivo in Vitoria. An eventful game with around 3.4 expected goals and the momentum changing hands more than once. Keep watching to the end – the closing stages matter. Worth it.
Rayo host Valencia in Vallecas, with a team from the top or bottom two involved. Very few chances – under 1.5 expected goals combined – and not much to report. One to skip.

Real Madrid against Celta at the Bernabéu, with a top-two side involved. Chances everywhere – more than five expected goals – plus a penalty, and it stays close into the final stages. Watch it in full.
The Seville derby. Around 2.8 expected goals, plenty of edge, and a game that stays close; the last quarter of an hour is the reason to watch. Worth a look for the atmosphere alone.
Villa host Sunderland, with a team from the top or bottom two involved. A tight game with very few chances – about 1.3 expected goals combined. Skip it.
Bournemouth against Forest. Plenty of chances – almost five expected goals between them – but as a contest it's average. The highlights will do.
Chelsea against Leeds, an old rivalry. Around 3.4 expected goals, a penalty and a game with real twists for a long spell. Worth watching, especially the first hour.

w: Stakes (top-two/bottom-two team, both top four/bottom four)
matches.sum: Two sides from the bottom four meet with plenty riding on it. Almost four expected goals between them and a game that refuses to settle: the momentum keeps shifting, and the final quarter of an hour is as lively as anything before it. A proper relegation scrap – worth watching in full.
City at home to Fulham. A competitive game with about 2.6 expected goals and both teams having their moments. Decent, but highlights are enough.

Newcastle host Arsenal at St James' Park, with a top-two side involved. A proper contest: around 3.2 expected goals, the momentum shifting, and the closing stages the best part. Worth watching in full.
Spurs at home to Ipswich. Around three expected goals, but the game never builds much tension. Highlights are enough.
Como against Cagliari on the lake. Few chances – about 1.2 expected goals combined – and little incident. Skip it.
Lazio host Lecce at the Olimpico, with a team from the top or bottom two involved. Not many chances and not much tension. Skip or watch the highlights.
Napoli against Torino at the Maradona. A close but cautious game with few real chances. Highlights only.
Parma host Roma. A wide-open game – around five expected goals – with the momentum changing hands more than once in the first hour. Worth watching.
Lugano against GC, with a team from the top or bottom two involved. Around three expected goals and a contest that stays close – the last fifteen minutes are the part to see. Worth it.
The Rhône derby in Sion. Around three expected goals, a goal ruled out and plenty of derby edge, but average as a match. Highlights recommended.
The Bernese derby at the Wankdorf, with a top-two side involved. Around 2.8 expected goals, the momentum keeps shifting and the closing stages are the highlight. Worth watching in full.
Augsburg against Mainz. Plenty of chances – around 5.2 expected goals combined – but as a contest it's average. The highlights will do.

The Nordderby: Werder, 6th, against Hamburg, 11th. Evenly matched on chances – both sides around 1.5 expected goals and close to 20 shots each – and the derby edge is there throughout. As a football match it's average rather than special: the highlights cover it well.
The Breton derby in Lorient. Around 2.7 expected goals, a penalty and a red card, and it stays close. A decent watch, especially for the derby edge.

Fourth-placed Marseille host Le Mans, 15th, at the Vélodrome. A wide-open game with more than five expected goals between the two sides, 30 shots and a penalty. It keeps building towards the end – one to watch in full.
Paris FC host Angers. Around four expected goals between them, but not much tension. Highlights are enough.

League leaders Barcelona at home to Villarreal, eighth. A busy, eventful afternoon: Barcelona take 30 shots, a penalty is awarded after a VAR review and two players are sent off. Very little about this one is predictable – watch it in full rather than in highlights.
A Madrid derby at Getafe. A busy afternoon: around 4.6 expected goals, a red card, a penalty and a VAR intervention. Lots of incident – the highlights pack it in well.
Osasuna against Málaga in Pamplona, with a team from the top or bottom two involved. A tight, scrappy game with a red card but few chances. Highlights only.
Racing host Real Sociedad at El Sardinero. One of the most open games of the round – almost seven expected goals – with a penalty and the momentum changing hands. Watch it in full.

Promoted Hull, 13th, host second-placed Brighton. A cagey game for long stretches, but not a quiet one: around four expected goals and 13 shots on target between the two sides, so both keepers have work to do. Stay with it to the end – the closing minutes are the most eventful part, a red card included.
Liverpool against Manchester United at Anfield. Lots of chances – around five expected goals – plus a red card, but it's average as a contest. Highlights are enough.

Twelfth-placed Atalanta against an Inter side sitting second. One of the most open games of the season so far: more than six expected goals combined, chances at both ends from the first quarter of an hour on, and two penalties. It never settles into a pattern – don't switch off before the final whistle.
Bologna host Udinese, with a team from the top or bottom two involved. A competitive game with around 3.7 expected goals and both sides having their spells. Decent viewing.
Juventus at home to Venezia, with a team from the top or bottom two involved. Around 2.7 expected goals and a penalty, but little tension. Highlights only.
Milan host Frosinone at San Siro. Around 3.5 expected goals and a VAR intervention, but not much of a contest. Highlights are enough.
Sassuolo against Genoa. Plenty of chances – almost four expected goals – but average overall. The highlights do the job.
Basel host Luzern at St. Jakob-Park. Around 2.7 expected goals; quiet for long stretches, but the closing stages pick up. Highlights, or the last twenty minutes.

Fifth against fourth at the Letzigrund – two direct rivals for the top four. Busy for both goalkeepers: 33 shots, 15 of them on target. It takes a while to get going, but the last twenty minutes are the reason to watch.
Lausanne against Vaduz with plenty at stake at the table's extremes. Around three expected goals, and the last fifteen minutes are the reason to watch. Worth it.

w: team in bottom 2 · both in bottom 4
matches.sum: Two sides from the bottom four meet, one of them in the bottom two. Not many chances, but the stakes are high and the final quarter of an hour is where it comes alive.
Brentford host Everton. A red card, but not much tension overall. Highlights only.
Monza against Fiorentina. Around 3.4 expected goals and a penalty, but little tension. Highlights are enough.
